claims.text: A threshold concentration of surface-segregated Cr or Al enables formation of a continuous, adherent oxide scale in multiprincipal-element alloys.
The protective oxide scale may consist of Cr2O3 or Al2O3.
A continuous, adherent Cr- or Al-rich oxide scale significantly retards oxidation.
Retarding oxidation through protective-scale formation preserves material integrity during sustained high-temperature exposure.
At high temperature, sufficient Cr or Al segregates to the alloy surface.
Surface-segregated Cr or Al oxidizes preferentially to form a protective layer.
The adherent oxide scale limits oxygen ingress.
The adherent oxide scale limits internal oxidation.
Limiting oxygen ingress and internal oxidation enhances oxidation resistance.
Limiting oxygen ingress and internal oxidation helps maintain structural integrity.
Above-threshold Cr or Al content will produce a lower oxidation rate than below-threshold content, observable as slower mass gain.
Above-threshold Cr or Al content will produce more uniform and adherent oxide scales than below-threshold content.
Above-threshold Cr or Al content will produce fewer oxide-scale spallation defects than below-threshold content.
Below-threshold Cr or Al content is expected to produce discontinuous or non-protective oxides.
Discontinuous or non-protective oxides lead to accelerated oxidation and degradation.
The hypothesized behavior is expected to hold from approximately 800°C to 1100°C in oxygen-rich atmospheres.
The governing behavior may differ at lower temperatures or in non-oxidizing environments.
